# gitmoap_group_provider_connection (Resource)

Stores, under a name, what a pipeline provider needs to reach an outside service, for use by pipelines in every repository beneath the group. A connection either holds static credentials, checked against the provider's credentials schema and stored encrypted, or names an identity to assume through OIDC federation, which stores no secret and works only with providers that support it. A connection's name is unique per provider within the group, and a group holds a limited number of connections, set by its plan. Answers `501` when this installation has no secret storage configured. Owners of the group.

The token needs `provider_connection:manage` and `provider_connection:read`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) Group id
- `name` (String)
- `provider_id` (String)

### Optional

- `auth_mode` (String) How a connection authenticates to its provider's cloud: `static_credentials` (stored
credentials, the default) or `oidc_federation` (nothing stored; each run assumes a cloud role
with a short-lived identity token gitmoap issues).
- `environment_ids` (List of String) Binds the connection to these environments, so only a step deploying to one of them may
use it. Each must be an environment the connection's pipelines can deploy to: one this
group or repository owns, a group above it, or — for a group's connection — a group or
repository beneath it. Leave it out to let any step use the connection. At most 20.
- `protected` (Boolean) Whether only a run on a protected branch or tag may use the connection: one a branch or
tag rule protects, building a commit in that ref's history. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--created_by))
- `environment_bound` (Boolean) Whether the connection is bound to environments. When it is, only a step deploying to one
of `environment_ids` may use it, and a connection bound only to environments since deleted
is usable by no step.
- `id` (String) Connection id
- `last_rotated_at` (String)
- `scope_id` (String)
- `scope_type` (String)
- `secret_refs` (Map of String) The names of the stored credential fields, each with a reference to where it is stored.
Never the values. Empty for an `oidc_federation` connection.

<a id="nestedatt--created_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `created_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by its group_id and id, joined with slashes.
terraform import gitmoap_group_provider_connection.example "<group_id>/<id>"
```
